cues: Nock's first sentence is his thesis: a marriage is much more than the sum of two spouses.
It is a relationship defined by legal, moral and conventional assumptions.
It is an institution, in the sociologist's sense: an established pattern of rules and roles, like the family, education or the economy, culturally patterned and tied to those other institutions.
Its rules come from outside any particular couple, and couples inherit them, as heirs to a vast system of understood principles.
